questions.title: Anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes
questions.subject: dev
questions.question: Which of the following critical chromosomal events occurs during anaphase I of meiosis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sister chromatid separation is the defining event of anaphase II (and of mitotic anaphase), not anaphase I; at anaphase I, sister chromatids remain joined at their centromere.
explanations.B: Correct. At anaphase I, the spindle pulls each pair of homologous chromosomes apart, sending one full, still-duplicated homologue to each pole — this is what makes meiosis I a reductional division, halving the chromosome number while sister chromatids stay together. It is only at the mechanically similar anaphase II, later, that sister chromatids are finally pulled apart from each other.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Chromosome uncoiling (decondensation) is a telophase event, occurring after the chromosomes have already reached the poles, not during the anaphase movement itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Nuclear envelope reformation is also a telophase event, following anaphase's chromosome movement, not occurring during anaphase I itself.

questions.learning_objective: State that homologous chromosomes separate at anaphase I of meiosis, while sister chromatids stay joined until they separate at anaphase II.
